usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/web/robots?domain=<host> (x402 paid, ~$0.005 USDC on Base; the `domain` query param is REQUIRED)
usage.outputShape: body.exists (bool), body.raw (robots.txt text or null), body.rules (per-user-agent allow/disallow map), body.sitemaps[] (sitemap URLs), body.crawl_delay (per-user-agent map), body.domain
quirks: The `domain` query param is REQUIRED but is NOT in the registry inputSchema (schema shows only {type:http,method:GET,discoverable:true}).
Calling the bare GET with no ?domain= returns HTTP 500 {"error":"Missing domain parameter"} AND STILL CHARGES the x402 fee — always include ?domain= or you lose money for nothing.
Pass `domain` as a bare host (e.g. example.com), not a full URL with scheme/path.
When a site has no robots.txt the call still succeeds 200 with exists:false and empty rules/sitemaps — that is a valid result, not an error.
Response includes a promotional `_hint` field unrelated to the result; ignore it.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/web/robots with a required `domain` query param set to the bare host you want to inspect (e.g. ?domain=example.com), not a full URL. It is a paid x402 endpoint (~$0.005 USDC on Base) — do NOT call it without the domain param or it returns 500 and still charges you. Read the parsed result from the JSON body: body.exists tells you if robots.txt was found, body.raw is the raw text, body.rules holds per-user-agent allow/disallow directives, body.sitemaps[] lists sitemap URLs, and body.crawl_delay holds crawl-delay values. A 200 with exists:false simply means the site has no robots.txt.
